newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends lower in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends lower in active trade.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar reversed early gains to close lower against its U.S. counterpart on Monday as the U.S. currency turned stronger against the yen in afternoon Tokyo trade, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$27.538, off an intraday high of T$27.487, against Saturday's T$27.501 close.
Turnover through dealers was an active US$211.5 million.
Dealers said looser liquidity in the domestic money market also helped the Taiwan dollar depreciation.
"Loose liquidity has made investors more willing to set up long U.S. dollar positions," said one dealer.
In late February, the Taiwan dollar rose from T$27.65 to around T$27.50 due to tight liquidity, which forced investors to sell U.S. dollars in exchange for Taiwan dollars.
Dealers saw a range of T$27.52-27.57 for Tuesday.
